skill_entry.name: 14. A new path, state, counter or option must be visible to the operator through the tools the team already uses
skill_entry.trigger: (a) Debug dump: new data members in a type whose HEAD print helper (debug_string, dump, to_string, operator<<) the diff leaves untouched. (b) Trace coverage: a new src/ file in a directory where no file contains TRACE_EVENT, plus an added function that loops over a container inside a lock scope or is named drain_*, expand_* or *_oom, with no trace macro added. (c) Exit-time counter: build-gated counters printed once from a static destructor while fuse_stats.hpp exists. (d) Launcher wiring: a new cxxopts row coupled by its parse to an option that a perfetto/ or bin/ launcher sets itself. (e) Sample output: a new perfetto::Category, TRACE_COUNTER, track or rendered report with no image, excerpt or capture location in the body.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Debug dump: list added members (and enum class lines). At HEAD bound the enclosing type, its helper and the helper body; grep each member; zero hits is a gap. 2. Trace: count TRACE_EVENT per sibling of the new src/ file; list added functions holding both a loop and a lock, or named drain_, expand_ or oom; drop register_, init_, setup_ functions; grep for the category header (context only). 3. Counter: a file with a gate hit (not TRON_FUSE_STATS_ENABLED) and a report hit; compare with fuse_stats.hpp on enable time, live read, interval. 4. Launcher: read the launcher exec line and usage for the coupled option. 5. Sample: grep the body for an image, code block or capture path.
skill_entry.question: Can an operator who runs the normal tools (the debug dump, a Perfetto trace, the FUSE stats tree, the launcher script) see, measure or switch on what this PR adds, today, without rebuilding or reading the source?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: Counters already registered in FUSE (PR 2980: Wade asked only about the atomics and the dump). A steady-state per-operation path: Wade closed his own PR 2713 question with "No action needed, just inquiring." before the author's 20 ns per operation reply. A new environment variable (tron-4353, 3879, 4596: no launcher ask). A merge or sync step of an existing branch (tron-1707, 1722, 1739 passed with a new untraced src/pos file). A one-time registration or init loop. A FUSE leaf, debug_string helper, dbg_* log line or test-output change as the subject of a sample ask (PR 2980, tron-1707, tron-1985 silent). A test-only knob or CMake test row. Never raise above a question: PR 4267 and 2713 were approved with it open.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Debug dump: "add these to the `<helper>` utility for printing?" Trace: "wouldn't it be useful to have some TRACE_EVENTs across <paths>? there is no `<subsystem>` category in perfetto.hpp either. No action needed, just asking." Counter: "I'm ok approving as-is, but did you look at using FUSE for this? collection could still be opt-in via env-var, then the counters could be read live and over chosen intervals." Launcher: "<script> is how people launch <binary> with <coupled flag>. So that script needs to take `<new flag>` and forward it (like it does other options today)." Sample: "do you have a couple screenshots of these new <captures> you could share?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit to normal, never blocking. His words: 'No action needed, just inquiring.' (3235915961); 'I'm ok approving this as-is, although' (5156698046); 'Just a nit... looks like it works well though.' (5106398334 part 1). The launcher gap is the one he states as a need ('that script needs an update'); it was met 1 h 32 min later (e4bcae9ded) and his approval followed at a head that contained the fix.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file (the print helper's body at HEAD); other files (the perfetto category header found by grep, h/system/fuse_stats.hpp, h/system/fuse_tronstats.hpp, README.stats.md, perfetto/tronperf and other launchers under bin/ and ci/, README.perfetto.md); PR body (for the sample); GitHub API for pre-rebase heads. Not CI, not runtime.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a new path, state, counter or option must be visible through the tools the team already uses

Setup additions for this check (the common setup's BASE formula fails on a merged PR, because the reviewed commit is then an ancestor of origin/main and `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself):

```
# BASE for a merged PR: the parent of the PR's first commit
BASE=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/commits --jq '.[0].parents[0].sha')
git -C WT merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main && echo merged   # records why the common formula was not used
# HEAD for an inline comment: the commit of the review that posted it (not the comment's own commit_id, which GitHub re-stamps)
gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/comments/<id> --jq '.commit_id[0:10] + " " + .original_commit_id[0:10] + " line=" + (.original_line|tostring)'
gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/reviews --jq '.[] | .submitted_at + " " + .commit_id[0:10] + " " + .state'
# HEAD for an issue comment: the last push before the comment time
gh api --paginate repos/positron-ai/tron/issues/N/timeline --jq '.[] | select(.event=="head_ref_force_pushed") | .created_at + " " + .commit_id[0:10]'
gh api 'repos/positron-ai/tron/compare/<last force-push sha>...<next review commit>' --jq '.commits[] | .sha[0:10] + " " + .commit.committer.date'   # regular pushes after the force push
# If git -C WT cat-file -t HEAD fails (pre-rebase commit), read files from GitHub and say so in the finding
gh api "repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<path>?ref=HEAD" --jq .content | base64 -d | grep -n -F -- '<flag>'
```

1. Debug dump. Added members: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*.hpp' | grep -n -E '^(\+\+\+|@@)|^\+\s+[^/(]+\s[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*(\s*=[^;]*|\{[^}]*\})?;'` (an added line with a type, a lowercase name, an optional initializer and a semicolon, no parenthesis); kind enums: `... | grep -n -E '^\+\s+enum (class )?'`. Take the type name from the `@@ ... struct <T> {` context. Bound the type and find its helper: `F=$(mktemp); git -C WT show HEAD:<file> > $F; S=$(grep -n -E "^(struct|class) <T>\b" $F | cut -d: -f1); E=$(awk -v s=$S 'NR>s && /^};/ {print NR; exit}' $F); sed -n "${S},${E}p" $F | grep -n -E 'std::string (debug_string|to_string|dump)\(|operator<<\('` (add S-1 to the printed line). Body end: `awk -v l=<helper line> 'NR>l && /^  }$/ {print NR; exit}' $F`. Then `sed -n '<helper>,<end>p' $F > body.txt; for m in <members>; do echo $m $(grep -c $m body.txt); done`. If the helper is only declared in the header, grep src/ for `<T>::debug_string(` and bound the body there. Zero hits for a state member = gap.
2. Trace coverage. New src files: `git -C WT diff --diff-filter=A --name-only BASE HEAD -- src`. For each new file's directory: `for f in $(git -C WT ls-tree --name-only HEAD <dir>); do echo "$f $(git -C WT show HEAD:$f | grep -c TRACE_EVENT)"; done`; continue only when every sibling is 0. Added functions holding both a loop and a lock: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- src h | awk '/^\+.*\)( const| noexcept)* \{$/ {fn=$0} /^\+.*for \(/ {loop[fn]=1} /^\+.*(lock_guard|unique_lock|scoped_lock)/ {lock[fn]=1} END {for (f in loop) if (lock[f]) print f}'`; also `grep -n -E '^\+.*(drain_|expand_|_oom)'`. Drop functions named register_*, init_* or setup_*, or called once from main or from a *_register_* path; state the caller of each hit. Added trace macros: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- src h | grep -c -E '^\+.*(TRACE_EVENT|TRACE_COUNTER|TRON_CHECKPOINT)'`. Category context: `git -C WT grep -l 'perfetto::Category(' HEAD -- h` (h/tron/perfetto.hpp before f3cc5baded of 2026-01-13, h/common/perfetto.hpp after) and list its names; if neither exists write Insufficient data. A missing category is context for the question, never a trigger.
3. Exit-time counter. Gate list: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD | grep -n -P '^\+.*(option\(TRON_|#ifdef TRON_(?!FUSE|PERFETTO)|#if TRON_)'`. Report list: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^\+.*(fprintf\(stderr|spdlog::(info|warn)\(.*count|report_at_exit|~[a-z_]+\(\) \{)'`. A file with hits in both lists is a candidate; a gate hit alone is not. For a candidate: `git -C WT show HEAD:README.stats.md | sed -n 1,40p`; `git -C WT show HEAD:h/system/fuse_stats.hpp | grep -n -E 'make_file|set_read_callback'`; `git -C WT show HEAD:h/system/fuse_tronstats.hpp | grep -n register_tronstats_metric_descriptor`; env-var precedent: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'getenv\("(TRON|RZ)_' HEAD -- h src | head`. Record the three axes (enable time, live read, interval). If README.stats.md or fuse_stats.hpp is absent at HEAD, write Insufficient data.
4. Launcher wiring. New option rows: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- src/runtron.cpp src/rinzler.cpp | grep -n -E '^\+\s*\("[a-z-]+",'`. Coupling: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- src/runtron.cpp src/rinzler.cpp | grep -n -E 'args.count\("|requires --|overrides'`; record the coupled option. Launchers: `git -C WT grep -n -E '"\$RUNTRON"|gen/runtron|bin/runtron' HEAD -- perfetto bin ci`; for each, `grep -n -F -- '--<coupled>'` on its exec line and usage (`sed -n '/^usage()/,/^}/p'`). If the launcher sets the coupled option and `git -C WT grep -n -F -- '--<new flag>' HEAD -- perfetto bin ci` is empty, that is the gap. Compile-time knobs: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^\+#define [A-Z_]+ [01]$'` are not launcher-reachable by construction; send one to step 3 only when it gates a counter or a report. A getenv addition never counts here. Do not demand a usage line for an option that stands alone (perfetto/tronperf names 4 of the 47 runtron options at main 2026-10-06).
5. Sample output. Only when the diff adds a `perfetto::Category(`, `TRACE_COUNTER`, a new track or annotation name, or a report format whose look a reader cannot predict from the code. Then `grep -n -E '!\[|\.png|\.pftrace|```|/scratch/|/var/tmp/|/home/' body.md`; an image, a decoded excerpt, a repository path or a named capture location (even a machine-local path, as on PR 3490) counts as a sample and closes the ask. Check 9 still reports a machine-local path as unusable to a GitHub reader; the two checks do not conflict. A FUSE leaf or a one-integer counter never needs a sample.
6. One question per gap, in the finding shape. Say it is not a condition of approval.

residual_risks: Sub-trigger (e) is needs_runtime for the remedy: an agent can detect the missing image but cannot produce a screenshot; the finding is the ask only.

The narrowed (b) requires a new src/ file; a walk-under-lock added to an existing untraced file does not fire. No corpus case shows Wade asking in that situation, so the narrowing follows the evidence, but it is a known blind spot.
The narrowed (d) requires option coupling; a stand-alone runtron option that a launcher documents siblings of never fires. Wade's only launcher ask was a coupled option, so the rule has n = 1.
Sub-trigger (c) reports Insufficient data when README.stats.md or h/system/fuse_stats.hpp is absent at HEAD (a PR on a base older than the FUSE layer).

Commits that only existed before a rebase (6e3f089cce, e4bcae9ded, 05f02a4863, 68ee3e206f on PR 3490) are absent from the worktree; the procedure reads them through gh api, which needs network access.
Step 3's gate grep uses `grep -P` (negative lookahead); on this host grep is ugrep, which accepts -P. Another host with a grep built without PCRE needs two greps and a `grep -v TRON_FUSE`.
Category count at 22b5e0d59c: own count 13 `perfetto::Category(` rows (14 at 3fd5edaa66 and main); the facts lens wrote 14 for 22b5e0d59c. Minor, not used by any step.

The silent corpus has 0 PRs that add a runtron cxxopts row and 0 that add an exit-time counter, so sub-triggers (c) and (d) have no negative-space test beyond the loud corpus; a latent false positive there cannot be excluded.
